name: google_shopping_camoufox
description: MEASURED 2026-09-18 (research/google_reopened_2026_09_18.json) -- this engine WORKS on Google today and its chromium twin does not. Crossing engine x host x egress one variable at a time: camoufox + www.google.com + the host's own egress returned a real SERP on 11 of 11 runs across four EN/RU queries, then 20 of 20 more at one request per ~15 s with no degradation. THAT ISOLATION WAS RUN ON WEB SEARCH, not on `udm=28`: this preset's own evidence is narrower -- the 09-17 sweep's single Google pass in 24 runs was google_shopping_camoufox/us, and the same recipe end to end on 09-18 returned 62 products with prices. THREE THINGS DECIDE IT. (1) Engine: chromium is refused on the same url, settings and egress, 3 of 3 -- the exact reverse of this repo's 2026-09-02 measurement, so do not trust an engine verdict older than a fortnight. (2) Host: every country ccTLD is refused even on the passing egress, including google.am from an Armenian exit, so it is the ccTLD itself and not a geo mismatch -- every locale here now builds www.google.com and carries the market in gl/hl instead. (3) Egress: our prem_res_rotating pool passed 1 of ~15, so `proxy_type` defaults to `none` on this twin, i.e. the scrape leaves from the server's own address. Override it if that is not what you want, and re-measure before assuming the pool is still refused. CONSEQUENCE OF THE EGRESS CHANGE, stated because nothing else says it: `proxy_type: none` resolves to DirectSession, whose max_attempts() is 1, so this preset is now SINGLE-ATTEMPT -- the rotate-on-block recovery it used to get (and which tests/presets/test_google_search_interstitial.py describes) cannot fire for this twin. A refusal is final on the first try. `proxy_country: GB` on `us` is shared with the chromium twin, which exits through the pool. On this twin's direct path `proxy_country` does not apply -- it steers an exit, and there is none -- so the materializer pins the market's own country (US: en-US) rather than the GB exit's en-GB/Europe/London over this host's Armenian address, and the zone follows this host (review on #136, 2026-09-22). Irrelevant, measured: block_assets (passes both ways), wait_until (load == networkidle), stealth, and session_type=sticky (one pass, then 0 of 7). SUPERSEDED 2026-09-18 -- the verdict below is the OPPOSITE of the one at the top of this description and is kept only as history; this engine is the one that carries the data now. Then: refused on every run -- 9 of 9 through the as-shipped config and two probes (tbm=shop with warmup; udm=28 without warmup), all ending on google.com/sorry (HTTP 200 or 429, blocked=True), while google_search_camoufox got through Google on 5 of 6 runs on the same day and google_shopping_chromium/us returned 55 rows: the Shopping vertical rejects this engine, not this URL or this warmup. Nothing in the preset changed that verdict at the time. It has since changed on Google's side: the 09-17 sweep's only Google pass in 24 runs was this preset (google_shopping_camoufox/us), and the 09-18 crossing put its chromium twin at 0 of 3 on the egress where camoufox passes. timeout_ms 45000 -> 34000 on 2026-09-05 (per-phase; see test_builtin_timeout_fits_the_first_attempt); the 45000 figures below are the 2026-08-28 state. Google Shopping tab (udm=28). Google's obfuscated class names change frequently (self_heal regenerates on drift). titles/prices are read per-card (div.PhALMc container) so they stay index-aligned; merchants is best-effort and may desync if a card omits the store; organic cards expose no per-card product URL (JS side-panel) so no url column is offered. Materializer lowercases country for gl= and derives lang for hl=. Product urls are NOT extractable: Google Shopping renders the cards with no <a href> at all (0 anchors across 55 live cards, 2026-07-26 — measured on Chromium, this preset's only engine before the 2026-08-27 split) and navigates via JS, so the field was removed rather than shipped permanently empty — an empty all=true field is not harmless, it trips row_alignment_mismatch on every successful run. ENGINE: Camoufox, fingerprint_profile=windows_on_host — a Windows claim over this host's real AMD GPU vendor. Windows rather than the honest Linux because measurement put an honest Linux claim at 15 and 23 retries against 1 and 8 for Windows (see src/browser/fingerprint_profile.py). MEASURED 2026-08-27 (n=2 per locale, 6 runs per engine, research/preset_audit_dual_engine_2026_08_27.json): THIS PRESET RETURNED NO DATA ON EITHER VARIANT — 0/6 runs each. This variant reached the requested …udm=28… URL on 4 of 6 runs (HTTP 200, block heuristic silent) and matched nothing there; the other 2 were sent to google.com/sorry/index. google_shopping_chromium ended at /sorry on 6/6 with all three retries spent. ROOT CAUSE SETTLED 2026-08-28 (task 5, by capture — verified independently on THIS preset, not assumed from google_search): the 4 reached-but-empty runs are the same JS bounce shell, confirmed live 2026-08-28 on this exact udm=28 URL (90,802 bytes, DE, the same `table,div,span,p{display:none}` marker as google_search's capture, 0 #rso / div.PhALMc matches) — `wait_until: domcontentloaded` returns before Google's client-side check redirects away from it. Measured live: `wait_until: load` plus `wait_for_selector: div.PhALMc.bVO81.lLi9V` (the same node `titles` already reads) leaves the shell and resolves the redirect for real — landing on either the populated tab or google.com/sorry depending on whether the exit passes Google's JS check. This splits into two distinct, correctly-classified outcomes instead of one silent success: if the redirect leaves the page stuck on this shell (URL unchanged, not a recognised block endpoint), `wait_for_selector` genuinely times out and raises `selector_not_found: div.PhALMc.bVO81.lLi9V`, which `is_selector_miss()` (src/queue/scrape_runner.py:132) treats as retry-worthy; if instead it lands on `google.com/sorry`, `redirected_to_block()` (src/browser/camoufox_runner.py:441, mirrored at src/browser/runner.py:1095) recognises the URL BEFORE `wait_for_selector` is ever called, skips the wait entirely (no extra latency over the old config), and the block classifier sets `blocked=True` with `"Captcha/block detected by heuristic"` — rotation then happens on `fetch_result.blocked` (src/queue/scrape_runner.py:646), not on a selector miss. Either way the old domcontentloaded-only config's single silent "0 rows, no error" stop is gone. Same shape and same fix as google_search (see that preset; also mirrors `yandex_search`'s wait_until=load + wait_for_selector). timeout_ms was already 45000 here, which already fits the 3-phase (warmup+goto+selector) budget at PAGE_TASK_TIMEOUT_S=120s on the fast-fail path (attempt 1 affordable ≈37.5s, shortened-and-logged, same arithmetic yandex_search runs on) but costs a real attempt in the pathological worst case: 3 phases each burning their full timeout afford only ONE full attempt before the 120s ceiling is spent (attempt 2 "not started"), where the old 2-phase config afforded two — a genuinely blocked run is not slower (see redirected_to_block above); only an ambiguously-stuck one pays the extra phase's time. This does NOT fix google_shopping_chromium's access block (6/6 at /sorry in the audit, for this preset alone) or guarantee a clean exit for Camoufox — this proxy pool's exit reputation drifts day to day. MEASURED 2026-08-28 (retest of the same twenty presets through the same harness after the five audit fixes; n=2 per locale, 92 runs, research/preset_audit_dual_engine_2026_08_28.json): 0/6 runs returned data, all six ending on google.com/sorry with blocked=True and "Captcha/block detected by heuristic" (5 at HTTP 200, 1 at 429), 3 retries each. Compare 08-27, where 4 of 6 reached .../search?q=...&udm=28 at HTTP 200 with the heuristic silent and still extracted 0 rows -- the interstitial shell passing as a clean fetch. The wait-strategy fix removed that silent outcome: every 0-row run here is now correctly labelled a block. ACCESS on this engine was worse than on its Chromium twin today (0/6 against 4/6), the reverse of 08-27 -- exit reputation, not an engine verdict at n=2. CALLER TIMEOUT, CONFIRMED: one attempt of this preset now costs ~36s -- every google run in the 08-28 record carries "attempt 1/3 shortened to ~36000ms of the requested 45000ms to fit the page-task ceiling" (measured 35.7-36.4s) -- and a job that spends all three attempts reached took_ms 59058 (google_search_chromium/us) and 57193 (google_search_camoufox/us), before any queue wait. `/api/v1/search?engine=google` answers from google_search_camoufox as its JS-SERP route (src/api/search.py, ENGINES) with no wait_until/wait_for_selector/timeout_ms override, so it inherits that twin's numbers verbatim, and yozh-law-checker's backend/app/services/scraper_search_client.py calls /api/v1/search with `timeout=60` and has four `return None` degrade paths. THAT CLIENT IS NOT AFFECTED TODAY: it calls the endpoint only with engine="yandex", which routes to yandex_search_camoufox and is untouched by this change. The consequence is conditional on that client switching to engine="google", at which point a blocked or retrying Google job legitimately outlives its 60s budget and the caller receives None with nothing to log, indistinguishable from an empty SERP. OPERATOR ACTION, IF AND WHEN THAT SWITCH HAPPENS: raise that client's timeout to at least 90s (clear of the 59.1s worst job measured here, still under PAGE_TASK_TIMEOUT_S=120s), or -- if 60s is a hard product constraint -- log the timeout degrade distinctly so "we gave up waiting" is never reported as "Google returned nothing".
